subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Follow-up after heart attack and stent placement
subjective.citation_text: Patient: I'm 68 years old and female. I came in today for a follow-up after my heart attack and stent placement. I just want to make sure I'm on the right track with my recovery and medications. Doctor: Could you please confirm if you have any known allergies or are currently taking any medications, including over-the-counter drugs or supplements? Patient: I don't have any allergies that I'm aware of. As for medications, I'm taking Brilinta twice a day, baby aspirin at night, and I also take Crestor 40 mg once a day. I was also prescribed Toprol 50 mg once a day. Doctor: Have you experienced any new or worsening symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath, dizziness, or fatigue since your heart attack and stent placement? Patient: I have had some shortness of breath when I go up and down stairs, but I haven't had any chest pain since the stent was placed. I feel better than I did right after the heart attack, but I'm still taking it easy and trying to follow my doctor's advice. Doctor: Have you experienced any dizziness, palpitations, or swelling in your legs or ankles recently? Patient: No, I haven't had any dizziness, palpitations, or swelling in my legs or ankles recently. I've been pretty steady since coming home from the hospital, just taking it easy and sticking to my medications. I do feel a little out of breath when I climb stairs, but nothing too bad. Doctor: Could you provide details about your physical examination findings, including vital signs, heart sounds, and any signs of fluid retention? Patient: My blood pressure was about 120/70 when I was in the office, which my doctor said was good. On my neck exam, there was no swelling or unusual sounds, and my heart had a slight murmur, but my lungs were clear. The site where they did the cardiac catheterization on my wrist looks good—no infection or swelling, and I can feel my pulse there. My doctor said everything

Doctor: Could you please confirm if you have any known allergies or are currently taking any medications, including over-the-counter drugs or supplements? Patient: I don't have any allergies that I'm aware of. As for medications, I'm taking Brilinta twice a day, baby aspirin at night, and I also take Crestor 40 mg once a day. I was also prescribed Toprol 50 mg once a day. Doctor: Have you experienced any new or worsening symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath, dizziness, or fatigue since your heart attack and stent placement? Patient: I have had some shortness of breath when I go up and down stairs, but I haven't had any chest pain since the stent was placed. I feel better than I did right after the heart attack, but I'm still taking it easy and trying to follow my doctor's advice. Doctor: Have you experienced any dizziness, palpitations, or swelling in your legs or ankles recently? Patient: No, I haven't had any dizziness, palpitations, or swelling in my legs or ankles recently. I've been pretty steady since coming home from the hospital, just taking it easy and sticking to my medications. I do feel a little out of breath when I climb stairs, but nothing too bad. Doctor: Could you provide details about your physical examination findings, including vital signs, heart sounds, and any signs of fluid retention? Patient: My blood pressure was about 120/70 when I was in the office, which my doctor said was good. On my neck exam, there was no swelling or unusual sounds, and my heart had a slight murmur, but my lungs were clear. The site where they did the cardiac catheterization on my wrist looks good—no infection or swelling, and I can feel my pulse there. My doctor said everything
